Below is a quick summary of what’s happening and a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* patch you can apply to get interpolation working inside `/…/`‐style regexes.

1. Bug root cause  
   In the second entry of the `regex` token for Ruby (the one matching `/…/`), there is no `inside` block, so `#{…}` is never re-tokenized as interpolation.

2. Fix  
   Add an `inside` definition (the same way the `%r{…}` pattern does) so that interpolation is highlighted.

```javascript
### components/prism-ruby.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
        {
            pattern: /(^|[^/])\/(?!\/)(?:\[[^\r\n\]]+\]|\\.|[^[/\\\r\n])+\/[gim]{0,3}(?=\s*(?:$|[\r\n,.;})]))/,
            lookbehind: true,
            greedy: true
        }
=======
        {
            pattern: /(^|[^/])\/(?!\/)(?:\[[^\r\n\]]+\]|\\.|[^[/\\\r\n])+\/[gim]{0,3}(?=\s*(?:$|[\r\n,.;})]))/,
            lookbehind: true,
            greedy: true,
            inside: {
                // enable #{…} interpolation inside /…/ regexes
                'interpolation': interpolation
            }
        }
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With that change, `/foo#{bar}/` will pick up the same `interpolation` tokens that `%r{foo#{bar}}` already does.
